data.one_liner: Schedule background work and execute Dart code on Android, iOS, macOS, Web, and Linux.
data.what_it_does: Allows scheduling and executing one-off or periodic background tasks in Flutter apps, even when the application is closed. It wraps native scheduling APIs across supported platforms like Android WorkManager and iOS Background Tasks.
use_when: You need to perform periodic data sync or cleanup tasks in the background
You need reliable file uploads or database maintenance while the app is closed
avoid_when: You need precise execution timing, which background schedulers cannot guarantee
You only need simple concurrent processing while the application is actively running
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, macOS, web, and Linux
Handles app closures and system reboots for scheduled tasks
Provides support for long-running tasks, progress updates, and work status observation
weaknesses: Background execution is subject to strict OS limitations and power management constraints
Experimental support for web and Linux has platform-specific limitations
data.setup_notes: Requires native platform setup for Android and iOS background execution as specified in the quick start guide.
